audit.whatIsWrong: The entry attributes Urgot's percent-max-health damage to his W throughout — "W shotgun legs", "his W cone", "they only fire in a short cone in front of him", "his percent-HP legs". Purge (W) is a 490-range channel that auto-attacks the nearest enemy at a fixed 3.0 attack speed for 4 seconds and applies on-hit at 50%. The leg shotguns are Echoing Flames, his PASSIVE, and each of the six legs carries its own cooldown of 30/20/10/5/2.5s by level.
audit.why: The distinction is the whole early lane. At level 1 each leg is on a thirty-second cooldown, so the max-health damage the text warns about barely exists yet; by levels 4-5 those cooldowns have fallen to 10-20 seconds and the same trade genuinely hurts. Bundling both into "his W" hides the one timing that tells you when the lane changes.
audit.corrected: Echoing Flames (P): six legs, 30/20/10/5/2.5s each by level, max-health damage. Purge (W): 490 range, 4s, 12/9/6/3/0s cooldown, triggers the legs.
sources: League Wiki — Urgot: Echoing Flames, Purge

audit.whatIsWrong: Packet defect: no cooldown-sequencing advice anywhere. Disdain is named as the thing to track but never given a number, a range, or a description of what it actually does to you.
audit.why: Disdain is a 450-unit dash on 16/15.5/15/14.5/14s that shields him, stuns for 1.5 seconds and then flings you 100 units behind him — into Purge range. It is his only mobility. Once it is spent, Urgot cannot close on or escape from anything for the next fourteen-plus seconds, which is the entire window Tahm Kench needs.
audit.corrected: Bait Disdain (16/15.5/15/14.5/14s, 450 units, 1.5s stun + flip); once it is gone he has no mobility, and Purge only reaches 490 against Tongue Lash's 900.

audit.whatIsWrong: Nothing notes that Disdain's stun cancels Abyssal Dive, in an entry whose full layer explicitly advises "W-dodge his E flip".
audit.why: Abyssal Dive channels for 1.35 seconds before it blinks. Disdain is a 1.5-second stun on a dash that closes 450 units. Trying to dodge the flip with W means starting a channel that his flip interrupts — the exact opposite of the advice given.
audit.corrected: Sidestep Disdain on foot. Abyssal Dive is what you spend after it has been baited, not the thing you dodge it with.
sources: League Wiki — Tahm Kench: Abyssal Dive (channel interrupted by immobilising and cast-inhibiting effects)

audit.whatIsWrong: wants.you[2], mid and whys[4] describe Tahm Kench's level 6 as "Abyssal Voyage" giving "global threat" that lets you "match any TP play globally".
audit.why: Tahm Kench has no global ability. His W is Abyssal Dive, a 1.35s channel into a 1000-1200 range blink. Level 6 in this lane is about Devour landing on a champion whose only mobility is one 450-unit dash — which is a far better reason to like level 6 than a global that does not exist.
audit.corrected: Level 6 is Devour against an immobile target. Teleport is what matches his map plays.
sources: League Wiki — Tahm Kench: Abyssal Dive

audit.whatIsWrong: spikes[1] and whys[2] both describe "stun into Devour" as the level-3 spike. Devour is the ultimate and arrives at 6.
audit.why: Level 3 is real, but what makes it real is the 1.5-second stun and the fact that Echoing Flames' legs are still on 30-second cooldowns — not a finisher the player has not unlocked.
audit.corrected: Level 3: three stacks, 1.5s stun, free auto chain against legs that are still on 30s cooldowns.

audit.whatIsWrong: spikes[3] says Urgot's "percent-max-HP scales with your tank stats".
audit.why: It scales with your maximum health, not with your resistances — armour and magic resist do reduce each hit, they simply cannot shrink the base. The same is true of Fear Beyond Death: its execute line sits at 25% of your MAXIMUM health, so a Heartsteel Tahm Kench has a larger absolute execute threshold than a squishier target, and a shield sitting on top of low health does not lift you over it.
audit.corrected: Echoing Flames and Fear Beyond Death both key off max health. Buying HP raises the absolute size of both; buying resistances still reduces what actually lands.
sources: League Wiki — Urgot: Echoing Flames, Fear Beyond Death

audit.why: The packet flagged "Fear Beyond Death's" as a probable wrong name — it is a false positive, that is the correct ultimate name with a possessive. The late paragraph's "roughly 25% HP" execute threshold and "will fire through your shields" are both accurate and were left alone.
sources: League Wiki — Urgot: Fear Beyond Death

edits.before: Levels 4-5 are the one honest danger window — Urgot's percent-max-HP legs tick for a meaningful chunk in a long trade, and without your ultimate you cannot disengage cleanly if he E-flips you inside his W cone. Play for stack fishing rather than extended brawls: Q to stack, bait the flip, sidestep it, and only commit the Devour all-in when three stacks are guaranteed. At level 6 Abyssal Voyage ends his ability to ignore the global board — match every TP, take Rift Herald, and keep him trapped in a losing lane rather than letting him roam to a fight where his kit is scarier.
edits.after: Levels 4-5 are the one honest danger window — Echoing Flames' leg cooldowns have dropped to 10-20 seconds each, so a long trade now genuinely hurts, and you have no ultimate yet if Disdain lands. That flip is a 450-unit dash on 16/15.5/15/14.5/14s: it stuns 1.5 seconds and then throws you 100 units behind him, into Purge range. Play for stack fishing rather than extended brawls: Q to stack, bait the flip, sidestep it on foot, and commit only on three stacks. At level 6 Devour arrives — and once Disdain is spent Urgot is one of the easiest champions in the game to swallow.
